title: LeMUR is now LLM Gateway: how to apply LLMs to transcripts
summary: LeMUR sunset on March 31, 2026, and LLM Gateway replaces it. This guide maps every LeMUR task (question-answer, summary, coaching, multi-transcript) to an LLM Gateway call, with working Python code.
body_markdown:
LeMUR, AssemblyAI's framework for running large language models over transcribed speech, sunset on March 31, 2026. Code that calls the LeMUR endpoints, or the SDK's` transcript.lemur` methods, no longer returns results.[LLM Gateway](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/llm-gateway) replaces it: one OpenAI-compatible API that runs 55+ models from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and open-model providers over your transcripts.


The workflow is the same two steps LeMUR hid behind one call. Transcribe the audio, then send the transcript text to a model with your prompt. This guide maps each LeMUR task to its LLM Gateway equivalent, with Python you can run today.


The full code is in the companion repo,[kelsey-aai/lemur-to-llm-gateway](https://github.com/kelsey-aai/lemur-to-llm-gateway) .


## What changed when LeMUR became LLM Gateway


LeMUR took transcript IDs and a prompt, picked from a small set of models, and handled the transcript for you. LLM Gateway is a general chat completions API. You send messages, you choose the model by its exact ID, and you decide what transcript text goes into the prompt.


LeMUR (sunset March 31, 2026) LLM Gateway


**Endpoint**` /lemur/v3/generate/task` plus summary, question-answer and action-items variants` POST https://llm-gateway.assemblyai.com/v1/chat/completions`


**Transcript input**` transcript_ids` (one or many) Transcript text in` messages` , or one` transcript_id` plus a` {{ transcript }}` tag


**Model choice** A short list set by` final_model` 55+ models by exact ID, such as` claude-sonnet-4-6` or` gemini-3.5-flash`


**Request format** LeMUR-specific fields (` prompt` ,` context` ,` answer_format` ) OpenAI-compatible chat completions, with structured outputs, tool calling and fallbacks


Two details matter most when you port code. First, there's no` transcript_ids` field, so questions across several files mean you combine the text yourself (covered below). Second, the model only sees the text you send. Speaker labels, timestamps and confidence scores don't come along unless you write them into the prompt.


## Step 1: Transcribe the audio with AssemblyAI-STT-3.7


Transcription works the same way it did under LeMUR. Use AssemblyAI-STT-3.7 for pre-recorded audio by setting` speech_models=\["assemblyai-stt-3-7"\]` . It's $0.21 per hour. Turn on speaker labels if your prompts need to know who said what.


```text
# pip install "assemblyai>=1.10.11"
import os


import assemblyai as aai


aai.settings.api_key = os.environ["ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY"]


config = aai.TranscriptionConfig(
speech_models=["assemblyai-stt-3-7"],
speaker_labels=True,
)
transcript = aai.Transcriber(config=config).transcribe("https://assembly.ai/wildfires.mp3")


if transcript.status == aai.TranscriptStatus.error:
raise RuntimeError(f"Transcription failed: {transcript.error}")


# LLM Gateway only sees the text you send, so put speaker labels in the text.
transcript_text = "\n".join(f"Speaker {u.speaker}: {u.text}" for u in transcript.utterances)
```


If you already have transcripts from your LeMUR days, you don't need to re-transcribe. Fetch them with` aai.Transcript.get_by_id("YOUR_TRANSCRIPT_ID")` and use their` text` .


## Step 2: Send the transcript to LLM Gateway


The Python SDK ships an` LLMGateway` client. Put your instructions in the system message and the transcript in the user message, then pick a model.


```text
gateway = aai.LLMGateway()


completion = gateway.chat.completions.create(
model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
messages=[
{"role": "system", "content": "Provide a brief summary of the transcript."},
{"role": "user", "content": f"Transcript:\n{transcript_text}"},
],
max_tokens=1000,
)


print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
print(completion.request_id)  # log this; support uses it to find the request
```


Prefer plain HTTP? The endpoint accepts the same body from any language. Here's the full flow with` requests` :


```text
import os
import time


import requests


HEADERS = {"authorization": os.environ["ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY"]}


# 1. Transcribe
response = requests.post(
"https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript",
headers=HEADERS,
json={"audio_url": "https://assembly.ai/wildfires.mp3", "speech_models": ["assemblyai-stt-3-7"]},
)
response.raise_for_status()
transcript_id = response.json()["id"]


while True:
transcript = requests.get(
f"https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript/{transcript_id}", headers=HEADERS
).json()
if transcript["status"] == "completed":
break
if transcript["status"] == "error":
raise RuntimeError(f"Transcription failed: {transcript['error']}")
time.sleep(3)


# 2. Prompt
response = requests.post(
"https://llm-gateway.assemblyai.com/v1/chat/completions",
headers=HEADERS,
json={
"model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
"messages": [
{"role": "system", "content": "Provide a brief summary of the transcript."},
{"role": "user", "content": f"Transcript:\n{transcript['text']}"},
],
"max_tokens": 1000,
},
)
response.raise_for_status()
print(response.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"])
```


There's a shortcut closer to LeMUR's behavior. Pass a top-level` transcript_id` and write` {{ transcript }}` in your first message, and LLM Gateway fills in the transcript's text before it runs the completion. It substitutes the plain` text` field only, once, and the tag has to match exactly, spaces included. Use it when you don't want to store transcripts on your side. Send the text yourself when you need speaker labels or more than one transcript.


Move Your LeMUR Prompts To LLM Gateway


One API key covers transcription and 55+ LLMs. Transcribe with AssemblyAI-STT-3.7, then run your prompts on the model that fits the task.

## Rebuild the three LeMUR tasks as prompts


The original LeMUR launch showed three jobs: answering questions about a call, writing a custom summary, and coaching a rep. LeMUR had dedicated endpoints for the first two. On LLM Gateway all three are prompts on the same endpoint, so you can version them, test them across models, and change the output format without waiting on an API.


```text
PROMPTS = {
# Was LeMUR question-answer
"qa": (
"Answer the question using only the transcript. "
"If the transcript doesn't contain the answer, say so.\n\n"
"Question: {question}"
),
# Was LeMUR custom summary
"summary": (
"Summarize this call for a sales manager in 5 bullet points. "
"Cover the customer's problem, the proposed solution, objections, and next steps."
),
# Was the LeMUR AI coach example
"coach": (
"You are a sales coach. Give the rep three specific suggestions to improve, "
"each with a short quote from the transcript that shows the moment to change."
),
}


def run_task(transcript_text: str, task: str, question: str = "") -> str:
completion = aai.LLMGateway().chat.completions.create(
model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
messages=[
{"role": "system", "content": PROMPTS[task].format(question=question)},
{"role": "user", "content": f"Transcript:\n{transcript_text}"},
],
max_tokens=1000,
)
return completion.choices[0].message.content


print(run_task(transcript_text, "qa", question="Did the customer agree to a follow-up?"))
```


LeMUR's` answer_format` and` answer_options` parameters have a better replacement too. If your next step is code, not a person, ask for JSON with[structured outputs](https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/llm-gateway/structured-outputs) and give the model a schema. Our comparison of the[best LLMs for extracting structured data from transcripts](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/best-llm-for-extracting-structured-data-from-transcripts) covers which models hold a schema reliably.


## Replace transcript_ids: ask one question across many transcripts


LeMUR's best trick was taking a list of transcript IDs and answering across all of them. LLM Gateway has no` transcript_ids` field. Fetch each transcript, label it, and send the combined text in one message.


```text
def combined_text(transcript_ids: list[str]) -> str:
sections = []
for i, transcript_id in enumerate(transcript_ids, start=1):
transcript = aai.Transcript.get_by_id(transcript_id)
sections.append(f'<call id="{i}" transcript_id="{transcript_id}">\n{transcript.text}\n</call>')
return "\n\n".join(sections)


completion = aai.LLMGateway().chat.completions.create(
model="gemini-3.5-flash",  # long-context model; check context_length in GET /v1/models
messages=[
{
"role": "system",
"content": "Across these calls, list the three most common customer objections. "
"Cite the call id for each.",
},
{"role": "user", "content": combined_text(["TRANSCRIPT_ID_1", "TRANSCRIPT_ID_2"])},
],
max_tokens=1500,
)
print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
```


Context length is the limit to watch. LeMUR advertised up to 10 hours of audio per request. With LLM Gateway, the ceiling is the model's context window, and the catalog lists it per model.` claude-sonnet-4-6` takes 200,000 tokens.` claude-opus-4-7` and` gemini-3.5-flash` take about 1 million. Call` GET https://llm-gateway.assemblyai.com/v1/models` to see` context_length` for every model before you batch a week of calls into one prompt.


Try Your Own Audio First


Upload a recording to the playground and check the transcript before you write a single prompt. The LLM can only be as good as the text you give it.

## Which model should replace your LeMUR model?


LeMUR picked from a handful of models. LLM Gateway gives you the whole[model catalog](https://www.assemblyai.com/products/llm-gateway/models) , so the right answer depends on transcript length and the task. Our[Voice Standard Bench results](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/best-llm-for-summarizing-transcripts) tested every Gateway model on real transcripts at four lengths. Small, fast models do well on short calls and fall off at meeting length, which our post on[small vs. large LLMs on transcripts](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/small-vs-large-llms-transcripts) breaks down.


Old LeMUR job Starting model on LLM Gateway Why


Summaries and Q&A on single calls` claude-sonnet-4-6` The model the docs use in their transcript examples; 200,000-token context; available in the EU


Many transcripts or long meetings in one request` gemini-3.5-flash` or` claude-opus-4-7` Context windows of about 1 million tokens


Short, high-volume cleanup and rewrites` qwen3.5-4b-32k-fast` A small model hosted by AssemblyAI, used in the docs quickstart; 32,768-token context


Treat this as a starting point and test on your own transcripts. Changing models is a one-string edit, and you can set[fallback models](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/how-to-add-automatic-llm-fallbacks-to-voice-pipeline) so a provider outage doesn't stop your pipeline.


## EU data residency


If your audio and prompts need to stay in the EU, keep both steps there. Transcribe on` api.eu.assemblyai.com` and send prompts to` https://llm-gateway.eu.assemblyai.com/v1/chat/completions` . The EU Gateway serves Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini models; OpenAI models run in the US region only. With the Python SDK, it's two settings:


```text
aai.settings.base_url = "https://api.eu.assemblyai.com"
aai.settings.llm_gateway_base_url = "https://llm-gateway.eu.assemblyai.com"
```


## LeMUR migration checklist


- Replace every call to a` /lemur/v3/` endpoint and every` transcript.lemur` or` aai.Lemur` SDK call with a chat completions request.
- Upgrade the Python SDK to 1.10.11 or later for` aai.LLMGateway` .
- Map your old` final_model` to an exact model ID from the catalog. Shorthand such as` claude-sonnet-4` is rejected; use` claude-sonnet-4-6` .
- Move` prompt` and` context` into a system message, and put the transcript in the user message.
- Replace` transcript_ids` lists with combined, labelled transcript text.
- Format utterances yourself if the prompt needs speaker labels. Our guide to[applying LLMs to multi-speaker audio](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/apply-llms-multi-speaker-audio) shows the patterns.
- Set` speech_models=\["assemblyai-stt-3-7"\]` on new transcription requests.
- Log the` request_id` from every response.
- Check billing. New accounts get $50 in free credits for the speech APIs, but LLM Gateway usage isn't covered, so add a payment method before you switch production traffic.


## What LLM Gateway adds that LeMUR didn't have


The move is more than a rename. You choose from 55+ models instead of a short list, and new models land in the catalog as they launch. Requests follow the OpenAI chat completions format, so existing OpenAI SDK code works by changing the base URL to` https://llm-gateway.assemblyai.com/v1` . Fallbacks, structured outputs, tool calling and prompt caching come with it. And because transcription and LLM calls share one API key and one dashboard, the pipeline LeMUR wrapped is still two calls to one vendor, with every step visible to you. For the full product overview, start with our[LLM Gateway guide](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/llm-gateway) . ## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)


### Is AssemblyAI LeMUR still available?


No. LeMUR sunset on March 31, 2026, and its endpoints no longer return results. LLM Gateway replaces it. You transcribe audio with AssemblyAI's speech-to-text API, then send the transcript text to` https://llm-gateway.assemblyai.com/v1/chat/completions` with a prompt and a model ID.


### Can AssemblyAI integrate with LLMs?


Yes, through LLM Gateway. It's an OpenAI-compatible API with 55+ models from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and open-model providers, on the same API key as transcription. You can pass transcript text in your messages, or pass a` transcript_id` and a` {{ transcript }}` tag to have the text inserted for you.


### Does AssemblyAI provide customizable summaries?


Yes. Summaries are prompts on LLM Gateway, so you control the length, format and focus, such as five bullets for a sales manager or a JSON object for your CRM. The older` summarization` and` auto_chapters` transcript parameters are deprecated in favor of this approach.


### How do I send multiple transcripts to an LLM with AssemblyAI?


Fetch each completed transcript, wrap each one in a labelled block, and send the combined text in one message. LLM Gateway has no` transcript_ids` field. Pick a model whose context window fits the total, such as` gemini-3.5-flash` or` claude-opus-4-7` at about 1 million tokens.


### Does LLM Gateway keep speaker labels from the transcript?


Only if you include them. When you use the` transcript_id` shortcut, LLM Gateway inserts the transcript's plain` text` field, without speakers or timestamps. To keep speaker labels, transcribe with` speaker_labels=True` and format the utterances into the prompt yourself.


### Is LLM Gateway included in the free tier?


No. New accounts get $50 in free credits for the speech APIs, and LLM Gateway usage isn't covered by them. You need an account with a payment method to call LLM Gateway.
